request: how does binary search find a number so fast?

beats.intent: A sorted array of 11 numbers as bars, 37 as the target
beats.narration: Here are eleven numbers in order. We want to find thirty seven.
beats.code:
stage.title("Binary search for 37")
arr = draw_array(stage, [3, 8, 12, 17, 23, 29, 37, 41, 50, 56, 63])
bars = arr[0] if len(arr) == 2 else arr

beats.intent: The middle bar, 29, lit; the left half through it greyed out
beats.narration: Look in the middle: twenty nine. Too small, so thirty seven must be to its right. Half the list is gone.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[5], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(*[bars[k].animate.set_opacity(0.15) for k in range(6)])
stage.caption("29 < 37: keep the right half")

beats.intent: The middle of what is left, 50, lit; it and everything right of it greyed
beats.narration: The middle of what is left is fifty. Too big: throw away it and everything after.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[8], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(*[bars[k].animate.set_opacity(0.15) for k in range(8, 11)])
stage.caption("50 > 37: keep the left part")

beats.intent: The bar 37 lit green after three looks
beats.narration: Two numbers left. The first one is thirty seven: found in three looks, not seven.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[6], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("Found in 3 looks")

beats.narration: Each look halves the list, so even a million numbers take only about twenty looks.
Four numbers, out of order: five, two, four, one.

beats.intent: First pass: 5 swaps past 2, 4 and 1 to the end
beats.narration: Compare neighbours and swap when the left is bigger. The five bubbles all the way to the end.
beats.code:
swap_bars(stage, arr, 0, 1)
swap_bars(stage, arr, 1, 2)
swap_bars(stage, arr, 2, 3)
stage.caption("Pass 1: 2, 4, 1, 5")

beats.narration: Second pass: two and four are fine, then four swaps past one.

beats.intent: Third pass: 2 swaps with 1, the bars in order 1, 2, 4, 5
beats.narration: Third pass: two swaps with one. Now everything is in order.

request: how does a map app find the shortest route?

beats.intent: A road network of five towns A to E with distances on each road
beats.narration: Five towns and the roads between them, each with its length in kilometres.
beats.code:
stage.title("The shortest route from A to E")
nodes = {"A": (-0.9, 0), "B": (-0.2, 0.75), "C": (-0.2, -0.75), "D": (0.5, 0.2), "E": (0.95, -0.4)}
edges = [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("C", "E"), ("D", "E")]
dots, roads = draw_network(stage, nodes, edges)
for road, km in zip(roads, [4, 2, 1, 5, 8, 10, 2]):
    upright = abs(road.get_start()[0] - road.get_end()[0]) < 0.3
    stage.label(road, str(km), direction=LEFT if upright else UP, color=GREY_A)

beats.intent: The route A-B-D-E lit in orange with its total 11
beats.narration: Going through B and D looks direct: four plus five plus two is eleven.
beats.code:
stage.play(*[roads[k].animate.set_color(ORANGE).set_stroke(width=6) for k in (0, 3, 6)])
stage.caption("A → B → D → E: 4 + 5 + 2 = 11 km")

beats.intent: The route A-C-B-D-E lit in green with its total 10
beats.narration: But detour through C first: two plus one plus five plus two is only ten.
beats.code:
stage.play(*[roads[k].animate.set_color(GREY_B).set_stroke(width=4) for k in (0, 3, 6)])
stage.play(*[roads[k].animate.set_color(GREEN).set_stroke(width=6) for k in (1, 2, 3, 6)])
stage.caption("A → C → B → D → E: 2 + 1 + 5 + 2 = 10 km")

beats.intent: The network beside the rule: always extend the closest town found so far
beats.narration: The app's trick is to grow outward from A, always from the closest town found so far, so it never misses a shorter detour.

request: how do you count to 13 in binary?

beats.intent: Four bit cells under 8 4 2 1 counting up from 0 to 13
beats.narration: With four switches worth eight, four, two and one, count up from zero.
beats.code:
stage.title("Counting in binary")
cells = count_binary(stage, bits=4, upto=13)

beats.narration: Thirteen is one eight, one four, no two and one one: one one zero one.

beats.intent: Bars of the 16 patterns 4 bits can make, 0 to 15
beats.narration: Four bits make sixteen patterns: zero up to fifteen. Each extra bit doubles that.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [2, 4, 8, 16], labels=["1 bit", "2 bits", "3 bits", "4 bits"])
stage.caption("Each bit doubles the count")
